4203     def set_index( 
4204         self, keys, drop=True, append=False, inplace=False, verify_integrity=False 
4205     ): 
4206         """ 
4207         Set the DataFrame index using existing columns. 
4208  
4209         Set the DataFrame index (row labels) using one or more existing 
4210         columns or arrays (of the correct length). The index can replace the 
4211         existing index or expand on it. 
4212  
4213         Parameters 
4214         ---------- 
4215         keys : label or array-like or list of labels/arrays 
4216             This parameter can be either a single column key, a single array of 
4217             the same length as the calling DataFrame, or a list containing an 
4218             arbitrary combination of column keys and arrays. Here, "array" 
4219             encompasses :class:`Series`, :class:`Index`, ``np.ndarray``, and 
4220             instances of :class:`~collections.abc.Iterator`. 
4221         drop : bool, default True 
4222             Delete columns to be used as the new index. 
4223         append : bool, default False 
4224             Whether to append columns to existing index. 
4225         inplace : bool, default False 
4226             Modify the DataFrame in place (do not create a new object). 
4227         verify_integrity : bool, default False 
4228             Check the new index for duplicates. Otherwise defer the check until 
4229             necessary. Setting to False will improve the performance of this 
4230             method. 
4231  
4232         Returns 
4233         ------- 
4234         DataFrame 
4235             Changed row labels. 
4236  
4237         See Also 
4238         -------- 
4239         DataFrame.reset_index : Opposite of set_index. 
4240         DataFrame.reindex : Change to new indices or expand indices. 
4241         DataFrame.reindex_like : Change to same indices as other DataFrame. 
4242  
4243         Examples 
4244         -------- 
4245         >>> df = pd.DataFrame({'month': [1, 4, 7, 10], 
4246         ...                    'year': [2012, 2014, 2013, 2014], 
4247         ...                    'sale': [55, 40, 84, 31]}) 
4248         >>> df 
4249            month  year  sale 
4250         0      1  2012    55 
4251         1      4  2014    40 
4252         2      7  2013    84 
4253         3     10  2014    31 
4254  
4255         Set the index to become the 'month' column: 
4256  
4257         >>> df.set_index('month') 
4258                year  sale 
4259         month 
4260         1      2012    55 
4261         4      2014    40 
4262         7      2013    84 
4263         10     2014    31 
4264  
4265         Create a MultiIndex using columns 'year' and 'month': 
4266  
4267         >>> df.set_index(['year', 'month']) 
4268                     sale 
4269         year  month 
4270         2012  1     55 
4271         2014  4     40 
4272         2013  7     84 
4273         2014  10    31 
4274  
4275         Create a MultiIndex using an Index and a column: 
4276  
4277         >>> df.set_index([pd.Index([1, 2, 3, 4]), 'year']) 
4278                  month  sale 
4279            year 
4280         1  2012  1      55 
4281         2  2014  4      40 
4282         3  2013  7      84 
4283         4  2014  10     31 
4284  
4285         Create a MultiIndex using two Series: 
4286  
4287         >>> s = pd.Series([1, 2, 3, 4]) 
4288         >>> df.set_index([s, s**2]) 
4289               month  year  sale 
4290         1 1       1  2012    55 
4291         2 4       4  2014    40 
4292         3 9       7  2013    84 
4293         4 16     10  2014    31 
4294         """ 
4295         inplace = validate_bool_kwarg(inplace, "inplace") 
4296         if not isinstance(keys, list): 
4297             keys = [keys] 
4298  
4299         err_msg = ( 
4300             'The parameter "keys" may be a column key, one-dimensional ' 
4301             "array, or a list containing only valid column keys and " 
4302             "one-dimensional arrays." 
4303         ) 
4304  
4305         missing: List[Optional[Hashable]] = [] 
4306         for col in keys: 
4307             if isinstance( 
4308                 col, (ABCIndexClass, ABCSeries, np.ndarray, list, abc.Iterator) 
4309             ): 
4310                 # arrays are fine as long as they are one-dimensional 
4311                 # iterators get converted to list below 
4312                 if getattr(col, "ndim", 1) != 1: 
4313                     raise ValueError(err_msg) 
4314             else: 
4315                 # everything else gets tried as a key; see GH 24969 
4316                 try: 
4317                     found = col in self.columns 
4318                 except TypeError: 
4319                     raise TypeError(f"{err_msg}. Received column of type {type(col)}") 
4320                 else: 
4321                     if not found: 
4322                         missing.append(col) 
4323  
4324         if missing: 
4325             raise KeyError(f"None of {missing} are in the columns") 
4326  
4327         if inplace: 
4328             frame = self 
4329         else: 
4330             frame = self.copy() 
4331  
4332         arrays = [] 
4333         names = [] 
4334         if append: 
4335             names = list(self.index.names) 
4336             if isinstance(self.index, ABCMultiIndex): 
4337                 for i in range(self.index.nlevels): 
4338                     arrays.append(self.index._get_level_values(i)) 
4339             else: 
4340                 arrays.append(self.index) 
4341  
4342         to_remove: List[Optional[Hashable]] = [] 
4343         for col in keys: 
4344             if isinstance(col, ABCMultiIndex): 
4345                 for n in range(col.nlevels): 
4346                     arrays.append(col._get_level_values(n)) 
4347                 names.extend(col.names) 
4348             elif isinstance(col, (ABCIndexClass, ABCSeries)): 
4349                 # if Index then not MultiIndex (treated above) 
4350                 arrays.append(col) 
4351                 names.append(col.name) 
4352             elif isinstance(col, (list, np.ndarray)): 
4353                 arrays.append(col) 
4354                 names.append(None) 
4355             elif isinstance(col, abc.Iterator): 
4356                 arrays.append(list(col)) 
4357                 names.append(None) 
4358             # from here, col can only be a column label 
4359             else: 
4360                 arrays.append(frame[col]._values) 
4361                 names.append(col) 
4362                 if drop: 
4363                     to_remove.append(col) 
4364  
4365             if len(arrays[-1]) != len(self): 
4366                 # check newest element against length of calling frame, since 
4367                 # ensure_index_from_sequences would not raise for append=False. 
4368                 raise ValueError( 
4369                     f"Length mismatch: Expected {len(self)} rows, " 
4370                     f"received array of length {len(arrays[-1])}" 
4371                 ) 
4372  
4373         index = ensure_index_from_sequences(arrays, names) 
4374  
4375         if verify_integrity and not index.is_unique: 
4376             duplicates = index[index.duplicated()].unique() 
4377             raise ValueError(f"Index has duplicate keys: {duplicates}") 
4378  
4379         # use set to handle duplicate column names gracefully in case of drop 
4380         for c in set(to_remove): 
4381             del frame[c] 
4382  
4383         # clear up memory usage 
4384         index._cleanup() 
4385  
4386         frame.index = index 
4387  
4388         if not inplace: 
4389             return frame 
4390  
4391     def reset_index( 
4392         self, 
4393         level: Optional[Union[Hashable, Sequence[Hashable]]] = None, 
4394         drop: bool = False, 
4395         inplace: bool = False, 
4396         col_level: Hashable = 0, 
4397         col_fill: Optional[Hashable] = "", 
4398     ) -> Optional["DataFrame"]: 
4399         """ 
4400         Reset the index, or a level of it. 
4401  
4402         Reset the index of the DataFrame, and use the default one instead. 
4403         If the DataFrame has a MultiIndex, this method can remove one or more 
4404         levels. 
4405  
4406         Parameters 
4407         ---------- 
4408         level : int, str, tuple, or list, default None 
4409             Only remove the given levels from the index. Removes all levels by 
4410             default. 
4411         drop : bool, default False 
4412             Do not try to insert index into dataframe columns. This resets 
4413             the index to the default integer index. 
4414         inplace : bool, default False 
4415             Modify the DataFrame in place (do not create a new object). 
4416         col_level : int or str, default 0 
4417             If the columns have multiple levels, determines which level the 
4418             labels are inserted into. By default it is inserted into the first 
4419             level. 
4420         col_fill : object, default '' 
4421             If the columns have multiple levels, determines how the other 
4422             levels are named. If None then the index name is repeated. 
4423  
4424         Returns 
4425         ------- 
4426         DataFrame or None 
4427             DataFrame with the new index or None if ``inplace=True``. 
4428  
4429         See Also 
4430         -------- 
4431         DataFrame.set_index : Opposite of reset_index. 
4432         DataFrame.reindex : Change to new indices or expand indices. 
4433         DataFrame.reindex_like : Change to same indices as other DataFrame. 
4434  
4435         Examples 
4436         -------- 
4437         >>> df = pd.DataFrame([('bird', 389.0), 
4438         ...                    ('bird', 24.0), 
4439         ...                    ('mammal', 80.5), 
4440         ...                    ('mammal', np.nan)], 
4441         ...                   index=['falcon', 'parrot', 'lion', 'monkey'], 
4442         ...                   columns=('class', 'max_speed')) 
4443         >>> df 
4444                  class  max_speed 
4445         falcon    bird      389.0 
4446         parrot    bird       24.0 
4447         lion    mammal       80.5 
4448         monkey  mammal        NaN 
4449  
4450         When we reset the index, the old index is added as a column, and a 
4451         new sequential index is used: 
4452  
4453         >>> df.reset_index() 
4454             index   class  max_speed 
4455         0  falcon    bird      389.0 
4456         1  parrot    bird       24.0 
4457         2    lion  mammal       80.5 
4458         3  monkey  mammal        NaN 
4459  
4460         We can use the `drop` parameter to avoid the old index being added as 
4461         a column: 
4462  
4463         >>> df.reset_index(drop=True) 
4464             class  max_speed 
4465         0    bird      389.0 
4466         1    bird       24.0 
4467         2  mammal       80.5 
4468         3  mammal        NaN 
4469  
4470         You can also use `reset_index` with `MultiIndex`. 
4471  
4472         >>> index = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples([('bird', 'falcon'), 
4473         ...                                    ('bird', 'parrot'), 
4474         ...                                    ('mammal', 'lion'), 
4475         ...                                    ('mammal', 'monkey')], 
4476         ...                                   names=['class', 'name']) 
4477         >>> columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples([('speed', 'max'), 
4478         ...                                      ('species', 'type')]) 
4479         >>> df = pd.DataFrame([(389.0, 'fly'), 
4480         ...                    ( 24.0, 'fly'), 
4481         ...                    ( 80.5, 'run'), 
4482         ...                    (np.nan, 'jump')], 
4483         ...                   index=index, 
4484         ...                   columns=columns) 
4485         >>> df 
4486                        speed species 
4487                          max    type 
4488         class  name 
4489         bird   falcon  389.0     fly 
4490                parrot   24.0     fly 
4491         mammal lion     80.5     run 
4492                monkey    NaN    jump 
4493  
4494         If the index has multiple levels, we can reset a subset of them: 
4495  
4496         >>> df.reset_index(level='class') 
4497                  class  speed species 
4498                           max    type 
4499         name 
4500         falcon    bird  389.0     fly 
4501         parrot    bird   24.0     fly 
4502         lion    mammal   80.5     run 
4503         monkey  mammal    NaN    jump 
4504  
4505         If we are not dropping the index, by default, it is placed in the top 
4506         level. We can place it in another level: 
4507  
4508         >>> df.reset_index(level='class', col_level=1) 
4509                         speed species 
4510                  class    max    type 
4511         name 
4512         falcon    bird  389.0     fly 
4513         parrot    bird   24.0     fly 
4514         lion    mammal   80.5     run 
4515         monkey  mammal    NaN    jump 
4516  
4517         When the index is inserted under another level, we can specify under 
4518         which one with the parameter `col_fill`: 
4519  
4520         >>> df.reset_index(level='class', col_level=1, col_fill='species') 
4521                       species  speed species 
4522                         class    max    type 
4523         name 
4524         falcon           bird  389.0     fly 
4525         parrot           bird   24.0     fly 
4526         lion           mammal   80.5     run 
4527         monkey         mammal    NaN    jump 
4528  
4529         If we specify a nonexistent level for `col_fill`, it is created: 
4530  
4531         >>> df.reset_index(level='class', col_level=1, col_fill='genus') 
4532                         genus  speed species 
4533                         class    max    type 
4534         name 
4535         falcon           bird  389.0     fly 
4536         parrot           bird   24.0     fly 
4537         lion           mammal   80.5     run 
4538         monkey         mammal    NaN    jump 
4539         """ 
4540         inplace = validate_bool_kwarg(inplace, "inplace") 
4541         if inplace: 
4542             new_obj = self 
4543         else: 
4544             new_obj = self.copy() 
4545  
4546         def _maybe_casted_values(index, labels=None): 
4547             values = index._values 
4548             if not isinstance(index, (PeriodIndex, DatetimeIndex)): 
4549                 if values.dtype == np.object_: 
4550                     values = lib.maybe_convert_objects(values) 
4551  
4552             # if we have the labels, extract the values with a mask 
4553             if labels is not None: 
4554                 mask = labels == -1 
4555  
4556                 # we can have situations where the whole mask is -1, 
4557                 # meaning there is nothing found in labels, so make all nan's 
4558                 if mask.all(): 
4559                     values = np.empty(len(mask)) 
4560                     values.fill(np.nan) 
4561                 else: 
4562                     values = values.take(labels) 
4563  
4564                     # TODO(https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/24206) 
4565                     # Push this into maybe_upcast_putmask? 
4566                     # We can't pass EAs there right now. Looks a bit 
4567                     # complicated. 
4568                     # So we unbox the ndarray_values, op, re-box. 
4569                     values_type = type(values) 
4570                     values_dtype = values.dtype 
4571  
4572                     if issubclass(values_type, DatetimeLikeArray): 
4573                         values = values._data 
4574  
4575                     if mask.any(): 
4576                         values, _ = maybe_upcast_putmask(values, mask, np.nan) 
4577  
4578                     if issubclass(values_type, DatetimeLikeArray): 
4579                         values = values_type(values, dtype=values_dtype) 
4580  
4581             return values 
4582  
4583         new_index = ibase.default_index(len(new_obj)) 
4584         if level is not None: 
4585             if not isinstance(level, (tuple, list)): 
4586                 level = [level] 
4587             level = [self.index._get_level_number(lev) for lev in level] 
4588             if len(level) < self.index.nlevels: 
4589                 new_index = self.index.droplevel(level) 
4590  
4591         if not drop: 
4592             to_insert: Iterable[Tuple[Any, Optional[Any]]] 
4593             if isinstance(self.index, ABCMultiIndex): 
4594                 names = [ 
4595                     (n if n is not None else f"level_{i}") 
4596                     for i, n in enumerate(self.index.names) 
4597                 ] 
4598                 to_insert = zip(self.index.levels, self.index.codes) 
4599             else: 
4600                 default = "index" if "index" not in self else "level_0" 
4601                 names = [default] if self.index.name is None else [self.index.name] 
4602                 to_insert = ((self.index, None),) 
4603  
4604             multi_col = isinstance(self.columns, ABCMultiIndex) 
4605             for i, (lev, lab) in reversed(list(enumerate(to_insert))): 
4606                 if not (level is None or i in level): 
4607                     continue 
4608                 name = names[i] 
4609                 if multi_col: 
4610                     col_name = list(name) if isinstance(name, tuple) else [name] 
4611                     if col_fill is None: 
4612                         if len(col_name) not in (1, self.columns.nlevels): 
4613                             raise ValueError( 
4614                                 "col_fill=None is incompatible " 
4615                                 f"with incomplete column name {name}" 
4616                             ) 
4617                         col_fill = col_name[0] 
4618  
4619                     lev_num = self.columns._get_level_number(col_level) 
4620                     name_lst = [col_fill] * lev_num + col_name 
4621                     missing = self.columns.nlevels - len(name_lst) 
4622                     name_lst += [col_fill] * missing 
4623                     name = tuple(name_lst) 
4624                 # to ndarray and maybe infer different dtype 
4625                 level_values = _maybe_casted_values(lev, lab) 
4626                 new_obj.insert(0, name, level_values) 
4627  
4628         new_obj.index = new_index 
4629         if not inplace: 
4630             return new_obj 
4631  
4632         return None

4653     def dropna(self, axis=0, how="any", thresh=None, subset=None, inplace=False): 
4654         """ 
4655         Remove missing values. 
4656  
4657         See the :ref:`User Guide <missing_data>` for more on which values are 
4658         considered missing, and how to work with missing data. 
4659  
4660         Parameters 
4661         ---------- 
4662         axis : {0 or 'index', 1 or 'columns'}, default 0 
4663             Determine if rows or columns which contain missing values are 
4664             removed. 
4665  
4666             * 0, or 'index' : Drop rows which contain missing values. 
4667             * 1, or 'columns' : Drop columns which contain missing value. 
4668  
4669             .. versionchanged:: 1.0.0 
4670  
4671                Pass tuple or list to drop on multiple axes. 
4672                Only a single axis is allowed. 
4673  
4674         how : {'any', 'all'}, default 'any' 
4675             Determine if row or column is removed from DataFrame, when we have 
4676             at least one NA or all NA. 
4677  
4678             * 'any' : If any NA values are present, drop that row or column. 
4679             * 'all' : If all values are NA, drop that row or column. 
4680  
4681         thresh : int, optional 
4682             Require that many non-NA values. 
4683         subset : array-like, optional 
4684             Labels along other axis to consider, e.g. if you are dropping rows 
4685             these would be a list of columns to include. 
4686         inplace : bool, default False 
4687             If True, do operation inplace and return None. 
4688  
4689         Returns 
4690         ------- 
4691         DataFrame 
4692             DataFrame with NA entries dropped from it. 
4693  
4694         See Also 
4695         -------- 
4696         DataFrame.isna: Indicate missing values. 
4697         DataFrame.notna : Indicate existing (non-missing) values. 
4698         DataFrame.fillna : Replace missing values. 
4699         Series.dropna : Drop missing values. 
4700         Index.dropna : Drop missing indices. 
4701  
4702         Examples 
4703         -------- 
4704         >>> df = pd.DataFrame({"name": ['Alfred', 'Batman', 'Catwoman'], 
4705         ...                    "toy": [np.nan, 'Batmobile', 'Bullwhip'], 
4706         ...                    "born": [pd.NaT, pd.Timestamp("1940-04-25"), 
4707         ...                             pd.NaT]}) 
4708         >>> df 
4709                name        toy       born 
4710         0    Alfred        NaN        NaT 
4711         1    Batman  Batmobile 1940-04-25 
4712         2  Catwoman   Bullwhip        NaT 
4713  
4714         Drop the rows where at least one element is missing. 
4715  
4716         >>> df.dropna() 
4717              name        toy       born 
4718         1  Batman  Batmobile 1940-04-25 
4719  
4720         Drop the columns where at least one element is missing. 
4721  
4722         >>> df.dropna(axis='columns') 
4723                name 
4724         0    Alfred 
4725         1    Batman 
4726         2  Catwoman 
4727  
4728         Drop the rows where all elements are missing. 
4729  
4730         >>> df.dropna(how='all') 
4731                name        toy       born 
4732         0    Alfred        NaN        NaT 
4733         1    Batman  Batmobile 1940-04-25 
4734         2  Catwoman   Bullwhip        NaT 
4735  
4736         Keep only the rows with at least 2 non-NA values. 
4737  
4738         >>> df.dropna(thresh=2) 
4739                name        toy       born 
4740         1    Batman  Batmobile 1940-04-25 
4741         2  Catwoman   Bullwhip        NaT 
4742  
4743         Define in which columns to look for missing values. 
4744  
4745         >>> df.dropna(subset=['name', 'born']) 
4746                name        toy       born 
4747         1    Batman  Batmobile 1940-04-25 
4748  
4749         Keep the DataFrame with valid entries in the same variable. 
4750  
4751         >>> df.dropna(inplace=True) 
4752         >>> df 
4753              name        toy       born 
4754         1  Batman  Batmobile 1940-04-25 
4755         """ 
4756         inplace = validate_bool_kwarg(inplace, "inplace") 
4757         if isinstance(axis, (tuple, list)): 
4758             # GH20987 
4759             raise TypeError("supplying multiple axes to axis is no longer supported.") 
4760  
4761         axis = self._get_axis_number(axis) 
4762         agg_axis = 1 - axis 
4763  
4764         agg_obj = self 
4765         if subset is not None: 
4766             ax = self._get_axis(agg_axis) 
4767             indices = ax.get_indexer_for(subset) 
4768             check = indices == -1 
4769             if check.any(): 
4770                 raise KeyError(list(np.compress(check, subset))) 
4771             agg_obj = self.take(indices, axis=agg_axis) 
4772  
4773         count = agg_obj.count(axis=agg_axis) 
4774  
4775         if thresh is not None: 
4776             mask = count >= thresh 
4777         elif how == "any": 
4778             mask = count == len(agg_obj._get_axis(agg_axis)) 
4779         elif how == "all": 
4780             mask = count > 0 
4781         else: 
4782             if how is not None: 
4783                 raise ValueError(f"invalid how option: {how}") 
4784             else: 
4785                 raise TypeError("must specify how or thresh") 
4786  
4787         result = self.loc(axis=axis)[mask] 
4788  
4789         if inplace: 
4790             self._update_inplace(result) 
4791         else: 
4792             return result 
4793  
4794     def drop_duplicates( 
4795         self, 
4796         subset: Optional[Union[Hashable, Sequence[Hashable]]] = None, 
4797         keep: Union[str, bool] = "first", 
4798         inplace: bool = False, 
4799         ignore_index: bool = False, 
4800     ) -> Optional["DataFrame"]: 
4801         """ 
4802         Return DataFrame with duplicate rows removed. 
4803  
4804         Considering certain columns is optional. Indexes, including time indexes 
4805         are ignored. 
4806  
4807         Parameters 
4808         ---------- 
4809         subset : column label or sequence of labels, optional 
4810             Only consider certain columns for identifying duplicates, by 
4811             default use all of the columns. 
4812         keep : {'first', 'last', False}, default 'first' 
4813             Determines which duplicates (if any) to keep. 
4814             - ``first`` : Drop duplicates except for the first occurrence. 
4815             - ``last`` : Drop duplicates except for the last occurrence. 
4816             - False : Drop all duplicates. 
4817         inplace : bool, default False 
4818             Whether to drop duplicates in place or to return a copy. 
4819         ignore_index : bool, default False 
4820             If True, the resulting axis will be labeled 0, 1, …, n - 1. 
4821  
4822             .. versionadded:: 1.0.0 
4823  
4824         Returns 
4825         ------- 
4826         DataFrame 
4827             DataFrame with duplicates removed or None if ``inplace=True``. 
4828         """ 
4829         if self.empty: 
4830             return self.copy() 
4831  
4832         inplace = validate_bool_kwarg(inplace, "inplace") 
4833         duplicated = self.duplicated(subset, keep=keep) 
4834  
4835         if inplace: 
4836             (inds,) = (-duplicated)._ndarray_values.nonzero() 
4837             new_data = self._data.take(inds) 
4838  
4839             if ignore_index: 
4840                 new_data.axes[1] = ibase.default_index(len(inds)) 
4841             self._update_inplace(new_data) 
4842         else: 
4843             result = self[-duplicated] 
4844  
4845             if ignore_index: 
4846                 result.index = ibase.default_index(len(result)) 
4847             return result 
4848  
4849         return None 
4850  
4851     def duplicated( 
4852         self, 
4853         subset: Optional[Union[Hashable, Sequence[Hashable]]] = None, 
4854         keep: Union[str, bool] = "first", 
4855     ) -> "Series": 
4856         """ 
4857         Return boolean Series denoting duplicate rows. 
4858  
4859         Considering certain columns is optional. 
4860  
4861         Parameters 
4862         ---------- 
4863         subset : column label or sequence of labels, optional 
4864             Only consider certain columns for identifying duplicates, by 
4865             default use all of the columns. 
4866         keep : {'first', 'last', False}, default 'first' 
4867             Determines which duplicates (if any) to mark. 
4868  
4869             - ``first`` : Mark duplicates as ``True`` except for the first occurrence. 
4870             - ``last`` : Mark duplicates as ``True`` except for the last occurrence. 
4871             - False : Mark all duplicates as ``True``. 
4872  
4873         Returns 
4874         ------- 
4875         Series 
4876         """ 
4877         from pandas.core.sorting import get_group_index 
4878         from pandas._libs.hashtable import duplicated_int64, _SIZE_HINT_LIMIT 
4879  
4880         if self.empty: 
4881             return Series(dtype=bool) 
4882  
4883         def f(vals): 
4884             labels, shape = algorithms.factorize( 
4885                 vals, size_hint=min(len(self), _SIZE_HINT_LIMIT) 
4886             ) 
4887             return labels.astype("i8", copy=False), len(shape) 
4888  
4889         if subset is None: 
4890             subset = self.columns 
4891         elif ( 
4892             not np.iterable(subset) 
4893             or isinstance(subset, str) 
4894             or isinstance(subset, tuple) 
4895             and subset in self.columns 
4896         ): 
4897             subset = (subset,) 
4898  
4899         #  needed for mypy since can't narrow types using np.iterable 
4900         subset = cast(Iterable, subset) 
4901  
4902         # Verify all columns in subset exist in the queried dataframe 
4903         # Otherwise, raise a KeyError, same as if you try to __getitem__ with a 
4904         # key that doesn't exist. 
4905         diff = Index(subset).difference(self.columns) 
4906         if not diff.empty: 
4907             raise KeyError(diff) 
4908  
4909         vals = (col.values for name, col in self.items() if name in subset) 
4910         labels, shape = map(list, zip(*map(f, vals))) 
4911  
4912         ids = get_group_index(labels, shape, sort=False, xnull=False) 
4913         return Series(duplicated_int64(ids, keep), index=self.index) 
4914

4918     @Substitution(**_shared_doc_kwargs) 
4919     @Appender(NDFrame.sort_values.__doc__) 
4920     def sort_values( 
4921         self, 
4922         by, 
4923         axis=0, 
4924         ascending=True, 
4925         inplace=False, 
4926         kind="quicksort", 
4927         na_position="last", 
4928         ignore_index=False, 
4929     ): 
4930         inplace = validate_bool_kwarg(inplace, "inplace") 
4931         axis = self._get_axis_number(axis) 
4932  
4933         if not isinstance(by, list): 
4934             by = [by] 
4935         if is_sequence(ascending) and len(by) != len(ascending): 
4936             raise ValueError( 
4937                 f"Length of ascending ({len(ascending)}) != length of by ({len(by)})" 
4938             ) 
4939         if len(by) > 1: 
4940             from pandas.core.sorting import lexsort_indexer 
4941  
4942             keys = [self._get_label_or_level_values(x, axis=axis) for x in by] 
4943             indexer = lexsort_indexer(keys, orders=ascending, na_position=na_position) 
4944             indexer = ensure_platform_int(indexer) 
4945         else: 
4946             from pandas.core.sorting import nargsort 
4947  
4948             by = by[0] 
4949             k = self._get_label_or_level_values(by, axis=axis) 
4950  
4951             if isinstance(ascending, (tuple, list)): 
4952                 ascending = ascending[0] 
4953  
4954             indexer = nargsort( 
4955                 k, kind=kind, ascending=ascending, na_position=na_position 
4956             ) 
4957  
4958         new_data = self._data.take( 
4959             indexer, axis=self._get_block_manager_axis(axis), verify=False 
4960         ) 
4961  
4962         if ignore_index: 
4963             new_data.axes[1] = ibase.default_index(len(indexer)) 
4964  
4965         if inplace: 
4966             return self._update_inplace(new_data) 
4967         else: 
4968             return self._constructor(new_data).__finalize__(self)

4970     def sort_index( 
4971         self, 
4972         axis=0, 
4973         level=None, 
4974         ascending: bool = True, 
4975         inplace: bool = False, 
4976         kind: str = "quicksort", 
4977         na_position: str = "last", 
4978         sort_remaining: bool = True, 
4979         ignore_index: bool = False, 
4980     ): 
4981         """ 
4982         Sort object by labels (along an axis). 
4983  
4984         Parameters 
4985         ---------- 
4986         axis : {0 or 'index', 1 or 'columns'}, default 0 
4987             The axis along which to sort.  The value 0 identifies the rows, 
4988             and 1 identifies the columns. 
4989         level : int or level name or list of ints or list of level names 
4990             If not None, sort on values in specified index level(s). 
4991         ascending : bool, default True 
4992             Sort ascending vs. descending. 
4993         inplace : bool, default False 
4994             If True, perform operation in-place. 
4995         kind : {'quicksort', 'mergesort', 'heapsort'}, default 'quicksort' 
4996             Choice of sorting algorithm. See also ndarray.np.sort for more 
4997             information.  `mergesort` is the only stable algorithm. For 
4998             DataFrames, this option is only applied when sorting on a single 
4999             column or label. 
5000         na_position : {'first', 'last'}, default 'last' 
5001             Puts NaNs at the beginning if `first`; `last` puts NaNs at the end. 
5002             Not implemented for MultiIndex. 
5003         sort_remaining : bool, default True 
5004             If True and sorting by level and index is multilevel, sort by other 
5005             levels too (in order) after sorting by specified level. 
5006         ignore_index : bool, default False 
5007             If True, the resulting axis will be labeled 0, 1, …, n - 1. 
5008  
5009             .. versionadded:: 1.0.0 
5010  
5011         Returns 
5012         ------- 
5013         sorted_obj : DataFrame or None 
5014             DataFrame with sorted index if inplace=False, None otherwise. 
5015         """ 
5016  
5017         # TODO: this can be combined with Series.sort_index impl as 
5018         # almost identical 
5019  
5020         inplace = validate_bool_kwarg(inplace, "inplace") 
5021  
5022         axis = self._get_axis_number(axis) 
5023         labels = self._get_axis(axis) 
5024  
5025         # make sure that the axis is lexsorted to start 
5026         # if not we need to reconstruct to get the correct indexer 
5027         labels = labels._sort_levels_monotonic() 
5028         if level is not None: 
5029  
5030             new_axis, indexer = labels.sortlevel( 
5031                 level, ascending=ascending, sort_remaining=sort_remaining 
5032             ) 
5033  
5034         elif isinstance(labels, ABCMultiIndex): 
5035             from pandas.core.sorting import lexsort_indexer 
5036  
5037             indexer = lexsort_indexer( 
5038                 labels._get_codes_for_sorting(), 
5039                 orders=ascending, 
5040                 na_position=na_position, 
5041             ) 
5042         else: 
5043             from pandas.core.sorting import nargsort 
5044  
5045             # Check monotonic-ness before sort an index 
5046             # GH11080 
5047             if (ascending and labels.is_monotonic_increasing) or ( 
5048                 not ascending and labels.is_monotonic_decreasing 
5049             ): 
5050                 if inplace: 
5051                     return 
5052                 else: 
5053                     return self.copy() 
5054  
5055             indexer = nargsort( 
5056                 labels, kind=kind, ascending=ascending, na_position=na_position 
5057             ) 
5058  
5059         baxis = self._get_block_manager_axis(axis) 
5060         new_data = self._data.take(indexer, axis=baxis, verify=False) 
5061  
5062         # reconstruct axis if needed 
5063         new_data.axes[baxis] = new_data.axes[baxis]._sort_levels_monotonic() 
5064  
5065         if ignore_index: 
5066             new_data.axes[1] = ibase.default_index(len(indexer)) 
5067  
5068         if inplace: 
5069             return self._update_inplace(new_data) 
5070         else: 
5071             return self._constructor(new_data).__finalize__(self) 
5072  
5073     def nlargest(self, n, columns, keep="first") -> "DataFrame": 
5074         """ 
5075         Return the first `n` rows ordered by `columns` in descending order. 
5076  
5077         Return the first `n` rows with the largest values in `columns`, in 
5078         descending order. The columns that are not specified are returned as 
5079         well, but not used for ordering. 
5080  
5081         This method is equivalent to 
5082         ``df.sort_values(columns, ascending=False).head(n)``, but more 
5083         performant. 
5084  
5085         Parameters 
5086         ---------- 
5087         n : int 
5088             Number of rows to return. 
5089         columns : label or list of labels 
5090             Column label(s) to order by. 
5091         keep : {'first', 'last', 'all'}, default 'first' 
5092             Where there are duplicate values: 
5093  
5094             - `first` : prioritize the first occurrence(s) 
5095             - `last` : prioritize the last occurrence(s) 
5096             - ``all`` : do not drop any duplicates, even it means 
5097                         selecting more than `n` items. 
5098  
5099             .. versionadded:: 0.24.0 
5100  
5101         Returns 
5102         ------- 
5103         DataFrame 
5104             The first `n` rows ordered by the given columns in descending 
5105             order. 
5106  
5107         See Also 
5108         -------- 
5109         DataFrame.nsmallest : Return the first `n` rows ordered by `columns` in 
5110             ascending order. 
5111         DataFrame.sort_values : Sort DataFrame by the values. 
5112         DataFrame.head : Return the first `n` rows without re-ordering. 
5113  
5114         Notes 
5115         ----- 
5116         This function cannot be used with all column types. For example, when 
5117         specifying columns with `object` or `category` dtypes, ``TypeError`` is 
5118         raised. 
5119  
5120         Examples 
5121         -------- 
5122         >>> df = pd.DataFrame({'population': [59000000, 65000000, 434000, 
5123         ...                                   434000, 434000, 337000, 11300, 
5124         ...                                   11300, 11300], 
5125         ...                    'GDP': [1937894, 2583560 , 12011, 4520, 12128, 
5126         ...                            17036, 182, 38, 311], 
5127         ...                    'alpha-2': ["IT", "FR", "MT", "MV", "BN", 
5128         ...                                "IS", "NR", "TV", "AI"]}, 
5129         ...                   index=["Italy", "France", "Malta", 
5130         ...                          "Maldives", "Brunei", "Iceland", 
5131         ...                          "Nauru", "Tuvalu", "Anguilla"]) 
5132         >>> df 
5133                   population      GDP alpha-2 
5134         Italy       59000000  1937894      IT 
5135         France      65000000  2583560      FR 
5136         Malta         434000    12011      MT 
5137         Maldives      434000     4520      MV 
5138         Brunei        434000    12128      BN 
5139         Iceland       337000    17036      IS 
5140         Nauru          11300      182      NR 
5141         Tuvalu         11300       38      TV 
5142         Anguilla       11300      311      AI 
5143  
5144         In the following example, we will use ``nlargest`` to select the three 
5145         rows having the largest values in column "population". 
5146  
5147         >>> df.nlargest(3, 'population') 
5148                 population      GDP alpha-2 
5149         France    65000000  2583560      FR 
5150         Italy     59000000  1937894      IT 
5151         Malta       434000    12011      MT 
5152  
5153         When using ``keep='last'``, ties are resolved in reverse order: 
5154  
5155         >>> df.nlargest(3, 'population', keep='last') 
5156                 population      GDP alpha-2 
5157         France    65000000  2583560      FR 
5158         Italy     59000000  1937894      IT 
5159         Brunei      434000    12128      BN 
5160  
5161         When using ``keep='all'``, all duplicate items are maintained: 
5162  
5163         >>> df.nlargest(3, 'population', keep='all') 
5164                   population      GDP alpha-2 
5165         France      65000000  2583560      FR 
5166         Italy       59000000  1937894      IT 
5167         Malta         434000    12011      MT 
5168         Maldives      434000     4520      MV 
5169         Brunei        434000    12128      BN 
5170  
5171         To order by the largest values in column "population" and then "GDP", 
5172         we can specify multiple columns like in the next example. 
5173  
5174         >>> df.nlargest(3, ['population', 'GDP']) 
5175                 population      GDP alpha-2 
5176         France    65000000  2583560      FR 
5177         Italy     59000000  1937894      IT 
5178         Brunei      434000    12128      BN 
5179         """ 
5180         return algorithms.SelectNFrame(self, n=n, keep=keep, columns=columns).nlargest() 
5181  
5182     def nsmallest(self, n, columns, keep="first") -> "DataFrame": 
5183         """ 
5184         Return the first `n` rows ordered by `columns` in ascending order. 
5185  
5186         Return the first `n` rows with the smallest values in `columns`, in 
5187         ascending order. The columns that are not specified are returned as 
5188         well, but not used for ordering. 
5189  
5190         This method is equivalent to 
5191         ``df.sort_values(columns, ascending=True).head(n)``, but more 
5192         performant. 
5193  
5194         Parameters 
5195         ---------- 
5196         n : int 
5197             Number of items to retrieve. 
5198         columns : list or str 
5199             Column name or names to order by. 
5200         keep : {'first', 'last', 'all'}, default 'first' 
5201             Where there are duplicate values: 
5202  
5203             - ``first`` : take the first occurrence. 
5204             - ``last`` : take the last occurrence. 
5205             - ``all`` : do not drop any duplicates, even it means 
5206               selecting more than `n` items. 
5207  
5208             .. versionadded:: 0.24.0 
5209  
5210         Returns 
5211         ------- 
5212         DataFrame 
5213  
5214         See Also 
5215         -------- 
5216         DataFrame.nlargest : Return the first `n` rows ordered by `columns` in 
5217             descending order. 
5218         DataFrame.sort_values : Sort DataFrame by the values. 
5219         DataFrame.head : Return the first `n` rows without re-ordering. 
5220  
5221         Examples 
5222         -------- 
5223         >>> df = pd.DataFrame({'population': [59000000, 65000000, 434000, 
5224         ...                                   434000, 434000, 337000, 11300, 
5225         ...                                   11300, 11300], 
5226         ...                    'GDP': [1937894, 2583560 , 12011, 4520, 12128, 
5227         ...                            17036, 182, 38, 311], 
5228         ...                    'alpha-2': ["IT", "FR", "MT", "MV", "BN", 
5229         ...                                "IS", "NR", "TV", "AI"]}, 
5230         ...                   index=["Italy", "France", "Malta", 
5231         ...                          "Maldives", "Brunei", "Iceland", 
5232         ...                          "Nauru", "Tuvalu", "Anguilla"]) 
5233         >>> df 
5234                   population      GDP alpha-2 
5235         Italy       59000000  1937894      IT 
5236         France      65000000  2583560      FR 
5237         Malta         434000    12011      MT 
5238         Maldives      434000     4520      MV 
5239         Brunei        434000    12128      BN 
5240         Iceland       337000    17036      IS 
5241         Nauru          11300      182      NR 
5242         Tuvalu         11300       38      TV 
5243         Anguilla       11300      311      AI 
5244  
5245         In the following example, we will use ``nsmallest`` to select the 
5246         three rows having the smallest values in column "a". 
5247  
5248         >>> df.nsmallest(3, 'population') 
5249                   population  GDP alpha-2 
5250         Nauru          11300  182      NR 
5251         Tuvalu         11300   38      TV 
5252         Anguilla       11300  311      AI 
5253  
5254         When using ``keep='last'``, ties are resolved in reverse order: 
5255  
5256         >>> df.nsmallest(3, 'population', keep='last') 
5257                   population  GDP alpha-2 
5258         Anguilla       11300  311      AI 
5259         Tuvalu         11300   38      TV 
5260         Nauru          11300  182      NR 
5261  
5262         When using ``keep='all'``, all duplicate items are maintained: 
5263  
5264         >>> df.nsmallest(3, 'population', keep='all') 
5265                   population  GDP alpha-2 
5266         Nauru          11300  182      NR 
5267         Tuvalu         11300   38      TV 
5268         Anguilla       11300  311      AI 
5269  
5270         To order by the largest values in column "a" and then "c", we can 
5271         specify multiple columns like in the next example. 
5272  
5273         >>> df.nsmallest(3, ['population', 'GDP']) 
5274                   population  GDP alpha-2 
5275         Tuvalu         11300   38      TV 
5276         Nauru          11300  182      NR 
5277         Anguilla       11300  311      AI 
5278         """ 
5279         return algorithms.SelectNFrame( 
5280             self, n=n, keep=keep, columns=columns 
5281         ).nsmallest() 
5282  
5283     def swaplevel(self, i=-2, j=-1, axis=0) -> "DataFrame": 
5284         """ 
5285         Swap levels i and j in a MultiIndex on a particular axis. 
5286  
5287         Parameters 
5288         ---------- 
5289         i, j : int or str 
5290             Levels of the indices to be swapped. Can pass level name as string. 
5291  
5292         Returns 
5293         ------- 
5294         DataFrame 
5295         """ 
5296         result = self.copy() 
5297  
5298         axis = self._get_axis_number(axis) 
5299  
5300         if not isinstance(result._get_axis(axis), ABCMultiIndex):  # pragma: no cover 
5301             raise TypeError("Can only swap levels on a hierarchical axis.") 
5302  
5303         if axis == 0: 
5304             assert isinstance(result.index, ABCMultiIndex) 
5305             result.index = result.index.swaplevel(i, j) 
5306         else: 
5307             assert isinstance(result.columns, ABCMultiIndex) 
5308             result.columns = result.columns.swaplevel(i, j) 
5309         return result 
5310  
5311     def reorder_levels(self, order, axis=0) -> "DataFrame": 
5312         """ 
5313         Rearrange index levels using input order. May not drop or duplicate levels. 
5314  
5315         Parameters 
5316         ---------- 
5317         order : list of int or list of str 
5318             List representing new level order. Reference level by number 
5319             (position) or by key (label). 
5320         axis : int 
5321             Where to reorder levels. 
5322  
5323         Returns 
5324         ------- 
5325         DataFrame 
5326         """ 
5327         axis = self._get_axis_number(axis) 
5328         if not isinstance(self._get_axis(axis), ABCMultiIndex):  # pragma: no cover 
5329             raise TypeError("Can only reorder levels on a hierarchical axis.") 
5330  
5331         result = self.copy() 
5332  
5333         if axis == 0: 
5334             assert isinstance(result.index, ABCMultiIndex) 
5335             result.index = result.index.reorder_levels(order) 
5336         else: 
5337             assert isinstance(result.columns, ABCMultiIndex) 
5338             result.columns = result.columns.reorder_levels(order) 
5339         return result 
5340  
5341     # ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
5342     # Arithmetic / combination related 
5343  
5344     def _combine_frame(self, other: "DataFrame", func, fill_value=None): 
5345         # at this point we have `self._indexed_same(other)` 
5346  
5347         if fill_value is None: 
5348             # since _arith_op may be called in a loop, avoid function call 
5349             #  overhead if possible by doing this check once 
5350             _arith_op = func 
5351  
5352         else: 
5353  
5354             def _arith_op(left, right): 
5355                 # for the mixed_type case where we iterate over columns, 
5356                 # _arith_op(left, right) is equivalent to 
5357                 # left._binop(right, func, fill_value=fill_value) 
5358                 left, right = ops.fill_binop(left, right, fill_value) 
5359                 return func(left, right) 
5360  
5361         if ops.should_series_dispatch(self, other, func): 
5362             # iterate over columns 
5363             new_data = ops.dispatch_to_series(self, other, _arith_op) 
5364         else: 
5365             with np.errstate(all="ignore"): 
5366                 res_values = _arith_op(self.values, other.values) 
5367             new_data = dispatch_fill_zeros(func, self.values, other.values, res_values) 
5368  
5369         return new_data 
5370  
5371     def _combine_match_index(self, other: Series, func): 
5372         # at this point we have `self.index.equals(other.index)` 
5373  
5374         if ops.should_series_dispatch(self, other, func): 
5375             # operate column-wise; avoid costly object-casting in `.values` 
5376             new_data = ops.dispatch_to_series(self, other, func) 
5377         else: 
5378             # fastpath --> operate directly on values 
5379             other_vals = other.values.reshape(-1, 1) 
5380             with np.errstate(all="ignore"): 
5381                 new_data = func(self.values, other_vals) 
5382             new_data = dispatch_fill_zeros(func, self.values, other_vals, new_data) 
5383         return new_data 
5384  
5385     def _construct_result(self, result) -> "DataFrame": 
5386         """ 
5387         Wrap the result of an arithmetic, comparison, or logical operation. 
5388  
5389         Parameters 
5390         ---------- 
5391         result : DataFrame 
5392  
5393         Returns 
5394         ------- 
5395         DataFrame 
5396         """ 
5397         out = self._constructor(result, index=self.index, copy=False) 
5398         # Pin columns instead of passing to constructor for compat with 
5399         #  non-unique columns case 
5400         out.columns = self.columns 
5401         return out 
5402  
5403     def combine( 
5404         self, other: "DataFrame", func, fill_value=None, overwrite=True 
5405     ) -> "DataFrame": 
5406         """ 
5407         Perform column-wise combine with another DataFrame. 
5408  
5409         Combines a DataFrame with `other` DataFrame using `func` 
5410         to element-wise combine columns. The row and column indexes of the 
5411         resulting DataFrame will be the union of the two. 
5412  
5413         Parameters 
5414         ---------- 
5415         other : DataFrame 
5416             The DataFrame to merge column-wise. 
5417         func : function 
5418             Function that takes two series as inputs and return a Series or a 
5419             scalar. Used to merge the two dataframes column by columns. 
5420         fill_value : scalar value, default None 
5421             The value to fill NaNs with prior to passing any column to the 
5422             merge func. 
5423         overwrite : bool, default True 
5424             If True, columns in `self` that do not exist in `other` will be 
5425             overwritten with NaNs. 
5426  
5427         Returns 
5428         ------- 
5429         DataFrame 
5430             Combination of the provided DataFrames. 
5431  
5432         See Also 
5433         -------- 
5434         DataFrame.combine_first : Combine two DataFrame objects and default to 
5435             non-null values in frame calling the method. 
5436  
5437         Examples 
5438         -------- 
5439         Combine using a simple function that chooses the smaller column. 
5440  
5441         >>> df1 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [0, 0], 'B': [4, 4]}) 
5442         >>> df2 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [1, 1], 'B': [3, 3]}) 
5443         >>> take_smaller = lambda s1, s2: s1 if s1.sum() < s2.sum() else s2 
5444         >>> df1.combine(df2, take_smaller) 
5445            A  B 
5446         0  0  3 
5447         1  0  3 
5448  
5449         Example using a true element-wise combine function. 
5450  
5451         >>> df1 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [5, 0], 'B': [2, 4]}) 
5452         >>> df2 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [1, 1], 'B': [3, 3]}) 
5453         >>> df1.combine(df2, np.minimum) 
5454            A  B 
5455         0  1  2 
5456         1  0  3 
5457  
5458         Using `fill_value` fills Nones prior to passing the column to the 
5459         merge function. 
5460  
5461         >>> df1 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [0, 0], 'B': [None, 4]}) 
5462         >>> df2 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [1, 1], 'B': [3, 3]}) 
5463         >>> df1.combine(df2, take_smaller, fill_value=-5) 
5464            A    B 
5465         0  0 -5.0 
5466         1  0  4.0 
5467  
5468         However, if the same element in both dataframes is None, that None 
5469         is preserved 
5470  
5471         >>> df1 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [0, 0], 'B': [None, 4]}) 
5472         >>> df2 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [1, 1], 'B': [None, 3]}) 
5473         >>> df1.combine(df2, take_smaller, fill_value=-5) 
5474             A    B 
5475         0  0 -5.0 
5476         1  0  3.0 
5477  
5478         Example that demonstrates the use of `overwrite` and behavior when 
5479         the axis differ between the dataframes. 
5480  
5481         >>> df1 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [0, 0], 'B': [4, 4]}) 
5482         >>> df2 = pd.DataFrame({'B': [3, 3], 'C': [-10, 1], }, index=[1, 2]) 
5483         >>> df1.combine(df2, take_smaller) 
5484              A    B     C 
5485         0  NaN  NaN   NaN 
5486         1  NaN  3.0 -10.0 
5487         2  NaN  3.0   1.0 
5488  
5489         >>> df1.combine(df2, take_smaller, overwrite=False) 
5490              A    B     C 
5491         0  0.0  NaN   NaN 
5492         1  0.0  3.0 -10.0 
5493         2  NaN  3.0   1.0 
5494  
5495         Demonstrating the preference of the passed in dataframe. 
5496  
5497         >>> df2 = pd.DataFrame({'B': [3, 3], 'C': [1, 1], }, index=[1, 2]) 
5498         >>> df2.combine(df1, take_smaller) 
5499            A    B   C 
5500         0  0.0  NaN NaN 
5501         1  0.0  3.0 NaN 
5502         2  NaN  3.0 NaN 
5503  
5504         >>> df2.combine(df1, take_smaller, overwrite=False) 
5505              A    B   C 
5506         0  0.0  NaN NaN 
5507         1  0.0  3.0 1.0 
5508         2  NaN  3.0 1.0 
5509         """ 
5510         other_idxlen = len(other.index)  # save for compare 
5511  
5512         this, other = self.align(other, copy=False) 
5513         new_index = this.index 
5514  
5515         if other.empty and len(new_index) == len(self.index): 
5516             return self.copy() 
5517  
5518         if self.empty and len(other) == other_idxlen: 
5519             return other.copy() 
5520  
5521         # sorts if possible 
5522         new_columns = this.columns.union(other.columns) 
5523         do_fill = fill_value is not None 
5524         result = {} 
5525         for col in new_columns: 
5526             series = this[col] 
5527             otherSeries = other[col] 
5528  
5529             this_dtype = series.dtype 
5530             other_dtype = otherSeries.dtype 
5531  
5532             this_mask = isna(series) 
5533             other_mask = isna(otherSeries) 
5534  
5535             # don't overwrite columns unnecessarily 
5536             # DO propagate if this column is not in the intersection 
5537             if not overwrite and other_mask.all(): 
5538                 result[col] = this[col].copy() 
5539                 continue 
5540  
5541             if do_fill: 
5542                 series = series.copy() 
5543                 otherSeries = otherSeries.copy() 
5544                 series[this_mask] = fill_value 
5545                 otherSeries[other_mask] = fill_value 
5546  
5547             if col not in self.columns: 
5548                 # If self DataFrame does not have col in other DataFrame, 
5549                 # try to promote series, which is all NaN, as other_dtype. 
5550                 new_dtype = other_dtype 
5551                 try: 
5552                     series = series.astype(new_dtype, copy=False) 
5553                 except ValueError: 
5554                     # e.g. new_dtype is integer types 
5555                     pass 
5556             else: 
5557                 # if we have different dtypes, possibly promote 
5558                 new_dtype = find_common_type([this_dtype, other_dtype]) 
5559                 if not is_dtype_equal(this_dtype, new_dtype): 
5560                     series = series.astype(new_dtype) 
5561                 if not is_dtype_equal(other_dtype, new_dtype): 
5562                     otherSeries = otherSeries.astype(new_dtype) 
5563  
5564             arr = func(series, otherSeries) 
5565             arr = maybe_downcast_to_dtype(arr, this_dtype) 
5566  
5567             result[col] = arr 
5568  
5569         # convert_objects just in case 
5570         return self._constructor(result, index=new_index, columns=new_columns) 
5571  
5572     def combine_first(self, other: "DataFrame") -> "DataFrame": 
5573         """ 
5574         Update null elements with value in the same location in `other`. 
5575  
5576         Combine two DataFrame objects by filling null values in one DataFrame 
5577         with non-null values from other DataFrame. The row and column indexes 
5578         of the resulting DataFrame will be the union of the two. 
5579  
5580         Parameters 
5581         ---------- 
5582         other : DataFrame 
5583             Provided DataFrame to use to fill null values. 
5584  
5585         Returns 
5586         ------- 
5587         DataFrame 
5588  
5589         See Also 
5590         -------- 
5591         DataFrame.combine : Perform series-wise operation on two DataFrames 
5592             using a given function. 
5593  
5594         Examples 
5595         -------- 
5596         >>> df1 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [None, 0], 'B': [None, 4]}) 
5597         >>> df2 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [1, 1], 'B': [3, 3]}) 
5598         >>> df1.combine_first(df2) 
5599              A    B 
5600         0  1.0  3.0 
5601         1  0.0  4.0 
5602  
5603         Null values still persist if the location of that null value 
5604         does not exist in `other` 
5605  
5606         >>> df1 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [None, 0], 'B': [4, None]}) 
5607         >>> df2 = pd.DataFrame({'B': [3, 3], 'C': [1, 1]}, index=[1, 2]) 
5608         >>> df1.combine_first(df2) 
5609              A    B    C 
5610         0  NaN  4.0  NaN 
5611         1  0.0  3.0  1.0 
5612         2  NaN  3.0  1.0 
5613         """ 
5614         import pandas.core.computation.expressions as expressions 
5615  
5616         def extract_values(arr): 
5617             # Does two things: 
5618             # 1. maybe gets the values from the Series / Index 
5619             # 2. convert datelike to i8 
5620             if isinstance(arr, (ABCIndexClass, ABCSeries)): 
5621                 arr = arr._values 
5622  
5623             if needs_i8_conversion(arr): 
5624                 if is_extension_array_dtype(arr.dtype): 
5625                     arr = arr.asi8 
5626                 else: 
5627                     arr = arr.view("i8") 
5628             return arr 
5629  
5630         def combiner(x, y): 
5631             mask = isna(x) 
5632             if isinstance(mask, (ABCIndexClass, ABCSeries)): 
5633                 mask = mask._values 
5634  
5635             x_values = extract_values(x) 
5636             y_values = extract_values(y) 
5637  
5638             # If the column y in other DataFrame is not in first DataFrame, 
5639             # just return y_values. 
5640             if y.name not in self.columns: 
5641                 return y_values 
5642  
5643             return expressions.where(mask, y_values, x_values) 
5644  
5645         return self.combine(other, combiner, overwrite=False) 
5646  
5647     def update( 
5648         self, other, join="left", overwrite=True, filter_func=None, errors="ignore" 
5649     ) -> None: 
5650         """ 
5651         Modify in place using non-NA values from another DataFrame. 
5652  
5653         Aligns on indices. There is no return value. 
5654  
5655         Parameters 
5656         ---------- 
5657         other : DataFrame, or object coercible into a DataFrame 
5658             Should have at least one matching index/column label 
5659             with the original DataFrame. If a Series is passed, 
5660             its name attribute must be set, and that will be 
5661             used as the column name to align with the original DataFrame. 
5662         join : {'left'}, default 'left' 
5663             Only left join is implemented, keeping the index and columns of the 
5664             original object. 
5665         overwrite : bool, default True 
5666             How to handle non-NA values for overlapping keys: 
5667  
5668             * True: overwrite original DataFrame's values 
5669               with values from `other`. 
5670             * False: only update values that are NA in 
5671               the original DataFrame. 
5672  
5673         filter_func : callable(1d-array) -> bool 1d-array, optional 
5674             Can choose to replace values other than NA. Return True for values 
5675             that should be updated. 
5676         errors : {'raise', 'ignore'}, default 'ignore' 
5677             If 'raise', will raise a ValueError if the DataFrame and `other` 
5678             both contain non-NA data in the same place. 
5679  
5680             .. versionchanged:: 0.24.0 
5681                Changed from `raise_conflict=False|True` 
5682                to `errors='ignore'|'raise'`. 
5683  
5684         Returns 
5685         ------- 
5686         None : method directly changes calling object 
5687  
5688         Raises 
5689         ------ 
5690         ValueError 
5691             * When `errors='raise'` and there's overlapping non-NA data. 
5692             * When `errors` is not either `'ignore'` or `'raise'` 
5693         NotImplementedError 
5694             * If `join != 'left'` 
5695  
5696         See Also 
5697         -------- 
5698         dict.update : Similar method for dictionaries. 
5699         DataFrame.merge : For column(s)-on-columns(s) operations. 
5700  
5701         Examples 
5702         -------- 
5703         >>> df = pd.DataFrame({'A': [1, 2, 3], 
5704         ...                    'B': [400, 500, 600]}) 
5705         >>> new_df = pd.DataFrame({'B': [4, 5, 6], 
5706         ...                        'C': [7, 8, 9]}) 
5707         >>> df.update(new_df) 
5708         >>> df 
5709            A  B 
5710         0  1  4 
5711         1  2  5 
5712         2  3  6 
5713  
5714         The DataFrame's length does not increase as a result of the update, 
5715         only values at matching index/column labels are updated. 
5716  
5717         >>> df = pd.DataFrame({'A': ['a', 'b', 'c'], 
5718         ...                    'B': ['x', 'y', 'z']}) 
5719         >>> new_df = pd.DataFrame({'B': ['d', 'e', 'f', 'g', 'h', 'i']}) 
5720         >>> df.update(new_df) 
5721         >>> df 
5722            A  B 
5723         0  a  d 
5724         1  b  e 
5725         2  c  f 
5726  
5727         For Series, it's name attribute must be set. 
5728  
5729         >>> df = pd.DataFrame({'A': ['a', 'b', 'c'], 
5730         ...                    'B': ['x', 'y', 'z']}) 
5731         >>> new_column = pd.Series(['d', 'e'], name='B', index=[0, 2]) 
5732         >>> df.update(new_column) 
5733         >>> df 
5734            A  B 
5735         0  a  d 
5736         1  b  y 
5737         2  c  e 
5738         >>> df = pd.DataFrame({'A': ['a', 'b', 'c'], 
5739         ...                    'B': ['x', 'y', 'z']}) 
5740         >>> new_df = pd.DataFrame({'B': ['d', 'e']}, index=[1, 2]) 
5741         >>> df.update(new_df) 
5742         >>> df 
5743            A  B 
5744         0  a  x 
5745         1  b  d 
5746         2  c  e 
5747  
5748         If `other` contains NaNs the corresponding values are not updated 
5749         in the original dataframe. 
5750  
5751         >>> df = pd.DataFrame({'A': [1, 2, 3], 
5752         ...                    'B': [400, 500, 600]}) 
5753         >>> new_df = pd.DataFrame({'B': [4, np.nan, 6]}) 
5754         >>> df.update(new_df) 
5755         >>> df 
5756            A      B 
5757         0  1    4.0 
5758         1  2  500.0 
5759         2  3    6.0 
5760         """ 
5761         import pandas.core.computation.expressions as expressions 
5762  
5763         # TODO: Support other joins 
5764         if join != "left":  # pragma: no cover 
5765             raise NotImplementedError("Only left join is supported") 
5766         if errors not in ["ignore", "raise"]: 
5767             raise ValueError("The parameter errors must be either 'ignore' or 'raise'") 
5768  
5769         if not isinstance(other, DataFrame): 
5770             other = DataFrame(other) 
5771  
5772         other = other.reindex_like(self) 
5773  
5774         for col in self.columns: 
5775             this = self[col]._values 
5776             that = other[col]._values 
5777             if filter_func is not None: 
5778                 with np.errstate(all="ignore"): 
5779                     mask = ~filter_func(this) | isna(that) 
5780             else: 
5781                 if errors == "raise": 
5782                     mask_this = notna(that) 
5783                     mask_that = notna(this) 
5784                     if any(mask_this & mask_that): 
5785                         raise ValueError("Data overlaps.") 
5786  
5787                 if overwrite: 
5788                     mask = isna(that) 
5789                 else: 
5790                     mask = notna(this) 
5791  
5792             # don't overwrite columns unnecessarily 
5793             if mask.all(): 
5794                 continue 
5795  
5796             self[col] = expressions.where(mask, this, that) 
5797  
5798     # ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
5799     # Data reshaping 
5800     @Appender( 
5801         """ 
5802 Examples 
5803 -------- 
5804 >>> df = pd.DataFrame({'Animal': ['Falcon', 'Falcon', 
5805 ...                               'Parrot', 'Parrot'], 
5806 ...                    'Max Speed': [380., 370., 24., 26.]}) 
5807 >>> df 
5808    Animal  Max Speed 
5809 0  Falcon      380.0 
5810 1  Falcon      370.0 
5811 2  Parrot       24.0 
5812 3  Parrot       26.0 
5813 >>> df.groupby(['Animal']).mean() 
5814         Max Speed 
5815 Animal 
5816 Falcon      375.0 
5817 Parrot       25.0 
5818  
5819 **Hierarchical Indexes** 
5820  
5821 We can groupby different levels of a hierarchical index 
5822 using the `level` parameter: 
5823  
5824 >>> arrays = [['Falcon', 'Falcon', 'Parrot', 'Parrot'], 
5825 ...           ['Captive', 'Wild', 'Captive', 'Wild']] 
5826 >>> index = pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays(arrays, names=('Animal', 'Type')) 
5827 >>> df = pd.DataFrame({'Max Speed': [390., 350., 30., 20.]}, 
5828 ...                   index=index) 
5829 >>> df 
5830                 Max Speed 
5831 Animal Type 
5832 Falcon Captive      390.0 
5833        Wild         350.0 
5834 Parrot Captive       30.0 
5835        Wild          20.0 
5836 >>> df.groupby(level=0).mean() 
5837         Max Speed 
5838 Animal 
5839 Falcon      370.0 
5840 Parrot       25.0 
5841 >>> df.groupby(level="Type").mean() 
5842          Max Speed 
5843 Type 
5844 Captive      210.0 
5845 Wild         185.0 
5846 """ 
5847     ) 
5848     @Appender(_shared_docs["groupby"] % _shared_doc_kwargs) 
5849     def groupby( 
5850         self, 
5851         by=None, 
5852         axis=0, 
5853         level=None, 
5854         as_index: bool = True, 
5855         sort: bool = True, 
5856         group_keys: bool = True, 
5857         squeeze: bool = False, 
5858         observed: bool = False, 
5859     ) -> "DataFrameGroupBy": 
5860         from pandas.core.groupby.generic import DataFrameGroupBy 
5861  
5862         if level is None and by is None: 
5863             raise TypeError("You have to supply one of 'by' and 'level'") 
5864         axis = self._get_axis_number(axis) 
5865  
5866         return DataFrameGroupBy( 
5867             obj=self, 
5868             keys=by, 
5869             axis=axis, 
5870             level=level, 
5871             as_index=as_index, 
5872             sort=sort, 
5873             group_keys=group_keys, 
5874             squeeze=squeeze, 
5875             observed=observed, 
5876         )

5878     _shared_docs[ 
5879         "pivot" 
5880     ] = """ 
5881         Return reshaped DataFrame organized by given index / column values. 
5882  
5883         Reshape data (produce a "pivot" table) based on column values. Uses 
5884         unique values from specified `index` / `columns` to form axes of the 
5885         resulting DataFrame. This function does not support data 
5886         aggregation, multiple values will result in a MultiIndex in the 
5887         columns. See the :ref:`User Guide <reshaping>` for more on reshaping. 
5888  
5889         Parameters 
5890         ----------%s 
5891         index : str or object, optional 
5892             Column to use to make new frame's index. If None, uses 
5893             existing index. 
5894         columns : str or object 
5895             Column to use to make new frame's columns. 
5896         values : str, object or a list of the previous, optional 
5897             Column(s) to use for populating new frame's values. If not 
5898             specified, all remaining columns will be used and the result will 
5899             have hierarchically indexed columns. 
5900  
5901             .. versionchanged:: 0.23.0 
5902                Also accept list of column names. 
5903  
5904         Returns 
5905         ------- 
5906         DataFrame 
5907             Returns reshaped DataFrame. 
5908  
5909         Raises 
5910         ------ 
5911         ValueError: 
5912             When there are any `index`, `columns` combinations with multiple 
5913             values. `DataFrame.pivot_table` when you need to aggregate. 
5914  
5915         See Also 
5916         -------- 
5917         DataFrame.pivot_table : Generalization of pivot that can handle 
5918             duplicate values for one index/column pair. 
5919         DataFrame.unstack : Pivot based on the index values instead of a 
5920             column. 
5921  
5922         Notes 
5923         ----- 
5924         For finer-tuned control, see hierarchical indexing documentation along 
5925         with the related stack/unstack methods. 
5926  
5927         Examples 
5928         -------- 
5929         >>> df = pd.DataFrame({'foo': ['one', 'one', 'one', 'two', 'two', 
5930         ...                            'two'], 
5931         ...                    'bar': ['A', 'B', 'C', 'A', 'B', 'C'], 
5932         ...                    'baz': [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], 
5933         ...                    'zoo': ['x', 'y', 'z', 'q', 'w', 't']}) 
5934         >>> df 
5935             foo   bar  baz  zoo 
5936         0   one   A    1    x 
5937         1   one   B    2    y 
5938         2   one   C    3    z 
5939         3   two   A    4    q 
5940         4   two   B    5    w 
5941         5   two   C    6    t 
5942  
5943         >>> df.pivot(index='foo', columns='bar', values='baz') 
5944         bar  A   B   C 
5945         foo 
5946         one  1   2   3 
5947         two  4   5   6 
5948  
5949         >>> df.pivot(index='foo', columns='bar')['baz'] 
5950         bar  A   B   C 
5951         foo 
5952         one  1   2   3 
5953         two  4   5   6 
5954  
5955         >>> df.pivot(index='foo', columns='bar', values=['baz', 'zoo']) 
5956               baz       zoo 
5957         bar   A  B  C   A  B  C 
5958         foo 
5959         one   1  2  3   x  y  z 
5960         two   4  5  6   q  w  t 
5961  
5962         A ValueError is raised if there are any duplicates. 
5963  
5964         >>> df = pd.DataFrame({"foo": ['one', 'one', 'two', 'two'], 
5965         ...                    "bar": ['A', 'A', 'B', 'C'], 
5966         ...                    "baz": [1, 2, 3, 4]}) 
5967         >>> df 
5968            foo bar  baz 
5969         0  one   A    1 
5970         1  one   A    2 
5971         2  two   B    3 
5972         3  two   C    4 
5973  
5974         Notice that the first two rows are the same for our `index` 
5975         and `columns` arguments. 
5976  
5977         >>> df.pivot(index='foo', columns='bar', values='baz') 
5978         Traceback (most recent call last): 
5979            ... 
5980         ValueError: Index contains duplicate entries, cannot reshape 
5981         """ 
5982  
5983     @Substitution("") 
5984     @Appender(_shared_docs["pivot"]) 
5985     def pivot(self, index=None, columns=None, values=None) -> "DataFrame": 
5986         from pandas.core.reshape.pivot import pivot 
5987  
5988         return pivot(self, index=index, columns=columns, values=values)
